context_notes: DURABLE LESSONS FROM THIS SESSION, in priority order. (1) THE ERROR MESSAGE DOES NOT DEFINE THE CLASS. I got R-B3 wrong THREE times (one test -> the checkout -> test-created fixtures) and the Trust CLI assertion TWICE, every time fixing what the log NAMED rather than what it IMPLIED. By contrast the fixes that held on the first attempt -- $LASTEXITCODE, ECHILD isolation, the class guard -- were all preceded by MECHANICAL ENUMERATION before any edit. Enumerate the class first; a CI log names one instance. (2) FAIL-FAST WAS HIDING A LOT. `cargo test --workspace` is fail-fast ACROSS targets, so nearly every 'new' red this session was pre-existing code that had NEVER executed in CI (nono-agentd, socket_access_run, the harness exit-code bug). Each fix unmasked the next layer. Verify 'masked' by grepping prior logs for ZERO occurrences -- do not assert it. (3) A truncating pipe can FAKE a verification: an early 'green' re-run was captured through `tail -35`, discarding the class guard's own result, and nearly passed unexamined. Capture FULL output when checking for PRESENCE rather than a final tally. (4) Windows takes a new object's owner from the CREATING TOKEN'S DEFAULT OWNER, not from the parent directory -- which is why owning %TEMP% could never fix test-created fixtures under elevation. (5) $LASTEXITCODE is native-only and `$null -ne 0` is True in PowerShell: the same confusion as 260815-f2x, inverted from fail-OPEN to fail-CLOSED. (6) Two ratified decisions can contradict each other indefinitely because each is only read in its own file (Cross.toml provisioned the very libdbus ci.yml asserted must be absent). (7) A reviewed rationale can rest on an unstated premise only one environment falsifies -- the receipt-sink guard's 'a redirect will be user-owned' was false under elevation. HOST GOTCHAS: this session is NON-ELEVATED, so icacls /setowner is a no-op and elevated-ownership fixes CANNOT be proven locally -- only CI can. `windows_run_*` live tests are ~20s each and a full env_vars sweep stalls; always filter. cross test needs ~8-20 min per cycle.
